_doctrine.purpose: Names with an ADJUDICATED court band but a coverage-orphaned (DEAD/THIN) put chain at/below that band -- where our own resting size IS the two-sided market, not a price-taker in someone else's liquidity.
three_edges: SPREAD edge: on a DEAD/THIN chain the quoted spread is a market-maker autoquote model, not a cleared price -- resting at/inside mid captures the spread instead of paying it, because there is no competing organic flow to outbid us.
STRIKE edge: every strike is anchored to an ADJUDICATED court band (never a chase) -- assignment, if it happens, buys us the stock AT OR BELOW a level the court has already underwritten as ownable.

CAPACITY edge: our own court-stated liquidity ceilings (VEL $10-15k, FSBW $8-12k, NATR starter-only, etc.) are the position's real capacity constraint, not the option chain's -- we are deliberately small enough that our own footprint cannot move the name, which is what keeps a coverage-orphaned chain durably ours to write.
five_program_rules: REST-NEVER-CROSS: always post the offer at or better than mid; never cross the spread to force a fill on a thin/dead chain -- a fast fill on a wide-spread thin chain is itself a red flag (see fill-speed diagnostic).
SELF-CANCEL: if unfilled and the underlying conditions have moved (band broken, a new event enters the tenor, court verdict downgraded) -- cancel and re-price rather than chase the old level.
ADVERSE-SELECTION FLAG: run the fill-speed diagnostic and counterparty inference (borrow/short-interest/13D-13G) on every name before writing and after every fill (see ADDENDUM below).

FLOAT-CAP ASSIGNMENT MATH: contracts sized so that full assignment never exceeds the court's own stated liquidity ceiling for the name -- translate the dollar ceiling into a hard max-contracts number before staging.

KILL-LINKED BTC PRICED AT FULL SPREAD: if a kill trigger fires, the buy-to-close is executed AT THE FULL OFFER (pay the spread) -- exits are urgency-priced, not patience-priced; never rest a closing order on a kill.

adverse_selection_addendum_20260803.context: Principal question: on a coverage-orphaned chain, who is on the other side of our offer -- a market-maker model, or a sharp? These rules are now part of the program, not just this build.
adverse_selection_addendum_20260803.fill_speed_diagnostic: Log time-to-fill on every trade. An offer LIFTED WITHIN MINUTES of posting = a market-maker model marked us cheap -> MANDATORY vol-input review before any further writes on that name (our IV/theoretical input was probably stale or wrong). An offer that RESTS DAYS before filling = organic flow found us at a fair level -- the good fill.
adverse_selection_addendum_20260803.counterparty_inference: Pre-write AND post-fill (re-check within 5 trading days of ANY fill): check (a) borrow fee/availability trend, (b) FINRA short volume, (c) any fresh 13D/13G on the name. A TIGHTENING BORROW = possible activist-short footprint on the other side of our put sale -> skip the write or halve size. Log the result as fill_forensics on the shadow-ledger row.
adverse_selection_addendum_20260803.mini_postmortem: EVERY FILL gets a mini-postmortem at +5 and +20 trading days: news? new filing? borrow move? The cohort's aggregate fill_forensics record is the program's own kill switch -- systematic adverse fills across the cohort self-terminates the program on its own data, no separate review needed.
adverse_selection_addendum_20260803.taxonomy_note: MM autoquotes are intermediaries, not sharps -- a fast autoquote lift is a pricing-input problem, not proof of an informed counterparty. The real adverse-counterparty risk in small paper is an ACTIVIST SHORT buying puts as a levered bear expression; this is detectable via the borrow/short-interest instruments the desk already runs, and is partially pre-screened by the honesty-channel courts (shared DNA with short-seller diligence process). FSBW's missed PWBK-acquisition catch (the court didn't surface the merger vote until the 08-03 adjudication, five months after it went public) is logged as the HUMILITY CASE for this taxonomy -- a name can clear every other program gate and still be running on a stale information set; counterparty inference is partly a hedge against our own coverage gaps, not just theirs.

demand_map_v2_correction_20260803.supersedes: the implicit v1 assumption that locked/concentrated sponsor holders are a plausible source of put-buying demand on these chains -- principal caught the hole; this correction governs the header and the ranking, not just a footnote.
why_concentrated_holders_are_mostly_excl: Standard IPO/secondary lockup agreements bar hedging outright ('no swap, hedge, or other arrangement transferring the economic consequences of ownership') -- locked sponsors/insiders CANNOT buy puts during their own unlock windows; they are legally the least likely counterparty, not the most likely.
Officer/director hedging is banned by near-universal post-Dodd-Frank company policy (Item 407(i) disclosure) independent of any lockup -- this persists even after the lockup itself expires.

Post-lockup affiliates face 16(c)/144 friction on options and typically exit via registered/block secondaries; their OTC hedge dealers (when a true institutional hedge exists) lay off risk in the STOCK, not in listed dead chains -- the flow never reaches our strikes.

demand_map.modal_buyer: BORROW-IMPAIRED BEARS -- informed directional shorts who can't get (or can't afford) stock borrow and buy puts as a synthetic short instead. This is the PRIMARY adverse-selection source on a coverage-orphaned chain, promoted from a secondary check to THE primary pre-write gate: run borrow-fee/availability + FINRA short-volume BEFORE sizing any write, not just as a post-fill diagnostic.
demand_map.unlock_event_flow: Real and dated, but THINNER and SMARTER than a sponsor-hedging assumption would imply -- unrestricted (non-affiliate, non-locked) holders and speculators trading the unlock date itself; SPCX's listed-put term structure around its lockup tranches is the on-file proof this flow exists. Treat as a secondary, event-timed demand source, not the modal one.
demand_map.pledge_carveout_lenders: The filings-verifiable NICHE source: lockups customarily carve out pledging sponsor stock as collateral for a bona fide loan, and the LENDER holding that pledge CAN hedge it (they are not the locked party). CENSUS FIELD ADDED per name: does the 424B4/S-1 lockup bar hedging outright, and does it carve out a pledge exception -- cite the specific lockup section. Material mainly for the sponsor-heavy recent-IPO names in this sweep (BOBS, APC, JMKE) and any name with disclosed insider share-pledging (VEL's 84% PE-controlled float + active Form-144 sell-down is the closest analog in this batch, though VEL itself is not a lockup situation).
demand_map.other: Post-news reactive flow (earnings/guide-cut/litigation) and non-affiliate funds running mechanical put-write/collar overlays -- both real, neither concentrated-holder-driven.

parameter_changes: LOWER expected fill rates across the board -- the buyer pool is thinner than a naive 'someone always wants insurance' prior assumed.

RAISE the required margin over Black-Scholes theoretical on any RESTING offer -- thin, informed-skewed demand means we should be paid MORE, not less, to supply liquidity; do not rest at a thin premium over theoretical just to improve fill odds.

RANK the inventory by demand-source quality, not just after-tax-carry x band-quality alone -- names with a verifiable pledge-carveout lender or a live unlock-event window rank ABOVE otherwise-equivalent 'sleepy value name nobody is trading' entries, because the former have an identifiable, explainable buyer on the other side and the latter may simply be untraded (adverse-selection-uncertain, not adverse-selection-clean).
demand_map_v2_correction_20260803.unchanged_foundation: An unfilled court-band put is still a free GTC order economically -- oversupplying resting offers costs ~nothing in itself. What changed is the EXPECTED VALUE if filled (lower fill probability, and a higher share of fills that DO happen are informed/adverse) -- this is a re-pricing of the tail, not a reason to stop writing.

IBKR's get_option_data endpoint (the strike-level chain tool that returns call/put contract IDs feeding OI/IV/marks) went systemically DOWN mid-sweep and NEVER RECOVERED this session -- confirmed via >30 combined retries across 4 parallel fork batches plus direct desk-session probes (control-tested on SPY and BKE, both failed identically). search_contracts, get_option_parameters (expiry lists), get_price_snapshot, and get_price_history all worked throughout. Every premium below is a BLACK-SCHOLES THEORETICAL (r=4%, sigma = the underlying's own IBKR 30-day historical_vol as an IV proxy, T = days-to-expiry/365) and is NOT a tradeable quote. This inventory is therefore a PRE-SCREEN: which names clear the band/economics/event bars well enough to be worth a live OI check the moment the endpoint recovers -- not an executable list. No staging occurred; nothing here is a live order. || UPDATE 2026-08-03 evening: outage recurrence #3 RECOVERED after ~30 min of polling in the dedicated recovery-watch session; OI verification completed for OMF/FAF/JMKE/MCHP/BOBS/TRU -- see oi_verification_20260803.
_doctrine.margin_over_theoretical_note: Per Demand Map v2 (parameter changes): thin, informed-skewed demand means we should be PAID MORE, not less, to supply a resting offer. The after-tax-annualized figures below are computed at RAW BS theoretical -- treat that as the floor, not the ask. Recommended resting limit = theoretical x ~1.10-1.20 (10-20% above raw BS fair value), scaled up further for any name without an identifiable demand-source (see demand_source field per candidate).

LADDER_SUPERSEDED_greedy_only_20260803.principal_challenge: 'why not: don't worry about the captive buyer, post the unfair lot only?'
LADDER_SUPERSEDED_greedy_only_20260803.VERDICT: CORRECT — the split ladder is superseded. My design had a queue-priority flaw I had not thought through.
LADDER_SUPERSEDED_greedy_only_20260803.the_flaw: in a lit book the buyer lifts the LOWEST offer first. Posting 3.50 alongside 4.40 does not discover the demand curve, it SUBSIDISES it: a buyer whose reservation is 4.40 takes the 3.50 lot first and pays an average of 3.95. Worked example, 2-lot buyer at 4.40 reservation: split ladder collects $790, two lots posted at 4.40 collect $880 — the split costs $90 to learn something we do not need.
LADDER_SUPERSEDED_greedy_only_20260803.why_the_information_argument_fails: the split was justified as 'mapping the demand curve'. But we do not need the curve — we need ONE BIT: does captivity clear ~1.9x fair? A single high offer answers exactly that bit. A no-fill is not a failed experiment, it is the answer (captivity is false at that price), and it costs nothing to learn.
LADDER_SUPERSEDED_greedy_only_20260803.cost_of_a_resting_unfilled_offer: ZERO — no margin encumbered until fill, no resting fee, GTC is free. The only 'cost' of the greedy-only post is foregone premium we were never owed.

LADDER_SUPERSEDED_greedy_only_20260803.what_replaces_the_ladder_as_the_experime: price-discovery by LADDERING IN TIME, not in the book: post high, and only if it sits unfilled for a defined window (say 10 sessions) step down 3.50-4.00. That sequence never leaves money on the table to a high-reservation buyer, and still finds the clearing price — it just finds it more slowly.
LADDER_SUPERSEDED_greedy_only_20260803.generalisation_for_the_program: on a dead chain we are the ONLY supply, so we face no queue competition from other sellers — but we DO face queue competition from ourselves. Never post two prices on the same strike simultaneously. One offer, at the top of the plausible range, stepped down over time.
LADDER_SUPERSEDED_greedy_only_20260803.supersedes: quote_structure_20260803 (split-offer discovery ladder) — that standard is WITHDRAWN for same-strike offers; it remains valid ACROSS strikes (65 and 70 simultaneously is fine, they are different instruments).
